name: EVA
aliases: Efficacy of VAginal oestrogen cream compared with placebo
question: Does perioperative vaginal oestriol cream improve patient-reported prolapse symptoms after primary native-tissue repair compared with placebo?

design.population: Postmenopausal women with POP-Q stage 2 or greater scheduled for primary native-tissue prolapse repair including anterior or posterior colporrhaphy.
design.locator: Owner PDF pp2–4, Methods and Results/Study Population, Figure 1

verdictNote: PGI-I improved; the observed difference was below the prespecified clinical relevance target.
takeaway: Perioperative vaginal oestriol cream improved 12-month patient-reported prolapse symptoms versus placebo after primary native-tissue repair (97/106 [91.5%] versus 83/104 [79.8%]; OR 2.73, 95% CI 1.18–6.28); composite surgical success did not differ significantly.

reports.label: Twelve-month randomized report
reports.citation: Vodegel EV, van Rest K, Speksnijder L, et al. "Vaginal Oestrogen Therapy for Postmenopausal Women Undergoing Prolapse Surgery: A Multicentre Double-Blind Randomised Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial." *BJOG.* Published online August 28, 2026. doi:10.1111/1471-0528.70311
reports.followUp: 12 months after surgery; 236/293 completed follow-up (57 dropouts) and 210 supplied the primary PGI-I response
reports.followUpLocator: Owner PDF p3, Results/Study Population; p5, Table 1

results.measure: Much or very much improved on PGI-I at 12 months
results.note: Two-sided superiority alpha 0.05; the observed risk difference was 11.7 percentage points, below the >15-point difference used in the clinical relevance and sample-size plan, which allowed 10% loss to follow-up.
results.locator: Owner PDF p3, Sample Size and Statistical Analysis; p5, Table 1 and note

results.measure: No prolapse beyond hymen, bulge symptoms, reoperation, or additional pessary therapy at 12 months
results.note: Composite definition combines anatomical, symptom and retreatment criteria.
results.locator: Owner PDF pp2–3, Secondary Outcomes; p5, Table 1 and note

results.measure: POP-Q cystocele stage 2 or greater at 12 months
Median PFDI-20 score at 12 months; lower indicates less distress
results.note: The paper reports a median difference of 8.3 points, not an arm-adjusted mean difference.
results.locator: Owner PDF pp4–5, Results and Table 1

results.measure: EQ-5D-5L discomfort/pain domain: no discomfort at 12 months
results.locator: Owner PDF pp4–5, Results and Table 1

results.measure: Vaginal pH 6 or lower at 12 months

delivery.label: Cream regimen
delivery.value: Oestriol 1 mg/g or matching placebo, 0.5 g intravaginally daily for 2 weeks then twice weekly, starting 4–6 weeks before surgery through 12 months after surgery with a planned 2-week postoperative pause.

delivery.label: Surgery and treatment initiation
delivery.value: 293/311 randomized participants underwent surgery and started the assigned intervention.

delivery.label: Operative approach
delivery.value: All included repairs required anterior or posterior colporrhaphy; 48% also had apical suspension by sacrospinous fixation or Manchester-Fothergill operation.
delivery.locator: Owner PDF p2, Methods/Participants; p7, Discussion/Interpretation

delivery.label: Per-protocol analysis
delivery.value: 185 participants met the adherence definition; the per-protocol findings were consistent with the main analysis.

relations.note: Both tested perioperative vaginal estrogen against placebo; EVA improved PGI-I after colporrhaphy, whereas IMPROVE found no PGI-I difference after apical repair.
